Keystrokes are 0 on both sides, so that metric is left out (#11). Ours is strictly better on steps, machine seconds and modelled seconds (human+wait 18.24 against 30.57).

The builder's path (Contacts > click a 'Government' tag button > Print or export > Excel, 4 steps, 0 keys) times out on the shared comparison dataset. No row on the first screen carries the tag: the grid renders 32 rows, and the first Government row is about the 139th by name (probe-tags.out, PageDown x7). It verifies only on verify's generated data (ours-health 4 steps/0 keys). The critic's driver (critic-ours-export-filtered-list.mjs) measures the builder's path and the round 1 path. The only path that verifies is Tags column options > Filter... > value > type 'Government' > Apply > Print or export > Excel: 6,581 rows, the same as Odoo. It is better on steps and seconds but ties on keystrokes (11 = 11). Not tie-accepted. (a) holds: ours is worse on no metric. (b) holds: the task tied in round 1 on this path. (c) fails: the decision record lists the paths tried but claims a 4-step, 0-key path instead of saying why ours cannot be shorter, and that path does not run on the comparison data. (d) holds: the critic found no winning path. Scrolling to a tag button takes at least 7 screens, so at least 11 steps. The filter popover offers no value suggestions. The list search does not match tags (0 results). The column menu has no sort. A tie is a loss.

biggest_gap.title: Exporting a filtered list still ties Odoo on keystrokes: the zero-typing tag-button path does not work on the comparison data
biggest_gap.detail: The round 2 shortcut only works when a row carrying the wanted tag happens to be on the first screen. A tag button in a row filters the list to that tag. On the shared 100,000-contact dataset sorted by name, the first 'Government' row is about the 139th, and the grid renders 32 rows, so the button is not there. The builder's ours driver times out after 120 s. It passed in verify only because ours-health runs on generated contacts. The only path that works is the round 1 one: Tags column options > Filter... > click the value > type 'Government' > Apply > Print or export > Excel. That is 8 steps and 11 keys against Odoo's 9 and 11, a tie on keystrokes and therefore a loss. The Tags filter has no list of values to pick from and no suggestions after a few letters, and the list search does not match tags. Fix: let the Tags filter offer the workspace's existing tag values as a pick list (or suggest them after one or two letters), so the tag is chosen rather than typed. For example: Tags options > Filter... > click 'Government' > Apply > Print or export > Excel, 0 keys. Also make the ours-health check of this task run on the comparison dataset.

[route: p14-import-export] The import and export isolation probe still only reads tenant B's exports, and A's download attack meets no finished, downloaded B file. In the plant, a download cache keyed by export id passed G1ImportExportAttackTests. G1ProcessStateTests (because the cache was static) and the module test TenantExportTests.After_one_workspace_downloaded... caught it. A cache that is not static (a singleton service, a file on disk) would be caught only by the module test. This is the same gap as round 1, not yet closed in the gate.

Full tenant export works now (fixed since round 1): the worker has the volume, 100,000-row workspaces export in 6 to 11 s, a failed export ends as failed with a reason and can be restarted, and the export holds companies, branches, users, roles, user roles and access, currencies, rates, custom field definitions, numbering sequences, saved views, contacts with custom-field columns and attachments with a sha256 manifest. Still missing for 'all of the tenant's data' (tenant-tables.txt): the audit trail (audit.entries, about 767,000 rows), numbering counters and issued numbers (needed to continue document numbering), the workspace's own record and settings (tenancy.tenants), user workplaces, jobs and job schedules.

The full export screen shows only a state word (Waiting / Ready) and no percentage or progress text. Progress exists only on the Background jobs screen. A finished import job's progress text still reads 'Checked 500 of 6000 rows.' at 100 % (big-import.out), unchanged from round 1.
The demo seeds a fake ready export ('1 file, 0 MB, CSV', download until 19/11/2036): a 10-year expiry next to the real 7-day ones.
Design system (p18): the export screen and the import mapping and duplicate choice still use native selects, and the export screen has no command bar (main select count 1, command bar 0).
Scope: still only contacts are registered for import. Users, companies, branches, currencies and custom field definitions cannot be imported through p14 (rates have their own import).

Duplicates (new this round, works in English and Arabic by keyboard): re-imported rows are warned about ('2 rows look like records that already exist'), with three choices (add, leave out, update). Update changes the right record and is audited. A row matching two contacts is refused ('matches more than one contact'). Two rows of the same file that duplicate each other are not flagged: both are created, duplicate count 0 (dupes.out).

Workspace rate for a foreign credit limit (new this round): it is used only when a rate exists within the age limit. The comparison dataset's rates end on 2026-09-30, so a USD row with no rate in the file is still refused. That is correct behaviour, but on old data the user is not told the workspace rate is too old.

List export works: CSV and XLSX in English and Arabic follow the current filter and the visible columns (City is Yiwu: 731 rows on screen and 731 in the file; the hidden Tags column is not in the file).
